frequency_question: How often do congressional principals successfully marshal the will and capability to pass a resolution of disapproval blocking a major executive-branch foreign/nuclear agreement within the statutory review window?
membership_rule: Includes formal privileged resolutions introduced under statutory review procedures (like the AECA or Atomic Energy Act) targeting major international agreements or arms sales; excludes non-binding resolutions and failed bills that lacked majority floor votes due to insufficient principal will.

cases.name: 1981 AWACS Saudi Arabia sale resolution of disapproval
1986 South Africa sanctions override (different mechanism, but related congressional override capability)
2017 Iran Nuclear Agreement review (Corker-Cardin / CRAA attempts)
2019 Yemen / Saudi arms sales joint resolutions of disapproval

coverage_note: 4 named major historical statutory review battles; captures the core base rate for legislative will versus executive agreements.
known_gaps: Excludes minor informal resolutions that never reached formal floor votes due to lack of leadership will.
skeleton: Legislative cycles involving statutory executive-agreement review where a congressional majority attempted to pass a blocking joint resolution: 4 major historical instances identified, with 1 successful override/passage past executive veto or successful bicameral passage without presidential acquiescence.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 4 major historical test cases.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks under the AECA and Atomic Energy Act remain stable across decades, though hyper-polarization affects will.
